entities.name: PMID:25452253
observations: Non-GM Brassica rapa × B. napus F1 hybrid and parental demographic rates were measured in agricultural and semi-natural habitats and modeled with crop rotation and outcrossing.
Hybrid population growth rate declined in both habitats; hybrids became extinct at two semi-natural sites.
Seed-bank survival had the greatest elasticity and was the main driver of persistence; agricultural persistence was projected for up to 20 years.
Hybrid persistence also depended on replenishment through outcrossing between B. rapa and B. napus.

entities.name: PMID:17971090
observations: In Québec field populations, B. napus-derived herbicide resistance persisted and introgressed into weedy B. rapa over six years without sustained herbicide selection.
Hybrid numbers declined from 85/approximately 200 plants in 2002 to 5/200 in 2005 at one site; an introgressed plant produced approximately 480 seeds.

entities.name: PMID:24889091
observations: In Dutch disturbed road-verge populations, F1 B. napus × B. rapa hybrids occurred where both species were close; recruitment likely involved the soil seed bank.
No evidence of recent crop-allele introgression into sampled wild B. rapa populations was detected.

entities.name: PMID:19278020
observations: In a field experiment with B. napus × B. juncea hybrids, hybrids had intermediate composite fitness and lowest reproductive fitness.
Hybrid progeny showed seed dormancy similar to the wild parent, and authors concluded dormancy and transgene effects could influence persistence.

entities.name: PMID:26175624
observations: Long-term surveys around Japanese ports found variable, site-specific trends in feral GM B. napus populations from spilled seed, with no common expansion or contraction trend.
No herbicide-tolerant B. juncea or B. rapa plants derived from crosses with GM B. napus were found.

entities.name: Seed bank controls hybrids
observations: For B. rapa × B. napus F1 hybrids, demographic elasticity analysis identified seed-bank survival as the strongest contributor to population growth rate in agricultural and semi-natural habitats.

entities.name: Replenishment controls persistence
observations: Hybrid persistence was jointly determined by parental seed-bank survival and replenishment through repeated outcrossing, so seed-bank dynamics are influential but not sufficient alone.
